papers.titleEn: Superposition Enhancement Effect of Dual Sensing Electrodes for Low-Temperature Solid-State Electrolyte NH3 Sensors
papers.abstract: To decrease the emission of hazardous NOx in iron and steel metallurgy and waste-to-energy incineration, it is crucial to develop solid-state electrolyte-based NH3 sensors compatible with the low-temperature selective catalytic reduction system. However, existing NH3 sensors require operating temperatures above 400 °C for stable operation and adequate sensitivity, which limits their use at 100-300 °C. Thus, the heterogeneous low-temperature SnO2/1% Co3O4 sensing electrode (SE) is developed and integrated with the CuV2O6 SE on a solid-state electrolyte for improving the sensitivity of solid electrolyte NH3 sensors at low operation temperature. The introduction of heterojunctions enhances the response signal of the SnO2/1% Co3O4 sensor in low-temperature ranges by reducing the interfacial charge transfer resistance associated with electrochemical reactions on the SE. Because of the superposition enhancement effect of SEs, the sensitivities of the SnO2/1% Co3O4-CuV2O6 sensor with two SEs increase by 93.5 and 72.8% on average compared to that of the SnO2/1% Co3O4 sensor and the CuV2O6 sensor respectively, and reach the largest sensitivity of -74.9 mV/decade at 200 °C. The developed SnO2/1% Co3O4-CuV2O6 sensor exhibits a calculated limit of detection of 0.14 ppm NH3, together with good anti-interference properties and stability. This work provides an effective way to develop low-temperature solid electrolyte gas sensors with large sensitivity.
papers.filename: Lei Dai, ACS Sens., 2026, Superposition Enhancement Effect of Dual Sensing Electrodes for Low-Temperature Solid-State Electrolyte NH3 Sensors

papers.titleEn: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
papers.abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl − induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Meng Li, Sci. Adv., 2026, Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells

papers.titleEn: Efficient UV-Curing Transfer Printing of Liquid-Metal/Ag-Nanowire Dual-Conductive Layers for Soft-Rigid Integrated Stretchable Electronics
papers.abstract: Liquid-metal-based stretchable electronics offer high conductivity and deformability, but efficient patterning, interfacial stability, and soft-rigid integration remain challenging. Here, we report an efficient UV-curing transfer printing strategy for liquid-metal microsphere/silver nanowire (LMMS/AgNW) dual-conductive layers. A tunable UV-curable resin provides adjustable elasticity, modulus, and adhesion. During transfer, the resin infiltrates the AgNW network and forms a semi-embedded interface after UV curing, while peeling-induced stress drives in situ rupture and coalescence of LMMS into continuous conductive pathways. Importantly, AgNWs act as a mechanically interlocked scaffold that anchors LMMS, mediates stress transfer, and maintains redundant electrical bridges during deformation. The resulting hierarchical structure, consisting of liquid-metal conductive pathways, LMMS reservoirs, and a semi-embedded AgNW network, enables high conductivity, strong interfacial adhesion, abrasion resistance, and stable resistance under large deformation. By modulating the same resin system, a chemically compatible hard-island/soft-sea platform was constructed for strain isolation and UV-assisted low-temperature bonding of rigid components. Deformable LED circuits and self-adhesive ECG/EMG electrodes demonstrate the potential of this integrated strategy for robust soft-rigid flexible electronics.
papers.filename: Jihai Zhang, Small, 2026, Efficient UV-Curing Transfer Printing of Liquid-Metal Ag-Nanowire Dual-Conductive Layers for Soft-Rigid Integrated Stretchable Electronics

papers.titleEn: Bifunctional Ligand Engineering of Aminophosphine-Derived InP Quantum Dots for Efficient Green Electroluminescence
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Tris(dimethylamino)phosphine ((DMA) 3 P)‐derived InP QDs commonly suffer from surface oxidation, undercoordinated surface atoms, and inefficient interfacial charge injection, which limit their optical and electroluminescent performance. Herein, we report a bifunctional ligand‐engineering strategy using phenethylamine (PEA) to simultaneously regulate the surface chemistry and interfacial electronic properties of green‐emitting InP QDs. The amine group of PEA coordinates to undercoordinated surface indium atoms, substantially suppressing InPO x ‐related surface species and passivating nonradiative trap states. Meanwhile, the short aromatic ligand structure promotes interfacial electronic coupling and facilitates charge injection into the QD emissive layer. Spectroscopic characterization and first‐principles calculations reveal the ligand‐induced charge redistribution and reduced surface traps. Consequently, PEA‐treated green InP QDs exhibit an improved photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 90%, compared with 73% for pristine InP QDs. The resulting green quantum‐dot light‐emitting diodes (QLEDs) show an increase in external quantum efficiency (EQE) from 5.08% to 11.5% following PEA treatment. Furthermore, the PEA‐treated devices achieve a maximum luminance of 7335 cd m − 2 and a T 50 operational lifetime of 10.8 h at an initial luminance of 100 cd m −2 . To the best of our knowledge, devices exhibit the highest luminance among previously reported (DMA) 3 P‐derived green InP QLEDs with a peak EQE exceeding 10%.
papers.filename: Soong Ju Oh, Small, 2026, Bifunctional Ligand Engineering of Aminophosphine-Derived InP Quantum Dots for Efficient Green Electroluminescence
